title: Contemplating G-d's unity: the general way, the particular way, and why each needs the other

lectures.id: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 044 ch 4 part 1.mp3
Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

overview: Chapter 4 asks how a person should contemplate the unity of G-d: by the general way, taking the whole at once, or by the particular way, taking one detail at a time. Each has an advantage. The general way reaches the depth of the essence, which transcends everything. The particular way brings that essence close, so that a person can feel it and point to it in his life. Each alone goes wrong. The general way by itself can leave someone sure that he is close to G-d when he is really far off, and the particular way can stop at a detail that is not G-dliness in itself. So the method is to go through the details, level by level, from the lower worlds up to *Atzilus*, and then gather them into one general *yichud*. The upper unity and the lower unity are treated the same way. The last part of the chapter turns to intention: the details serve the general point, and the words of davening, rightly understood, deepen the grasp of it. A newcomer should first deepen in the general way, and a person who prays should keep his intention on G-d Himself, not on His attributes.

terms.gloss: contemplation: a close, step-by-step study that makes an idea one's own
the particular way: contemplating through one detail or one example
contraction: the essence is contracted, limited and focused to become the *sefiros*
a particular unification: a yichud made on one particular thing
the general unification: the details gathered into one
self-nullification: the yesh nullified before G-d
greatness: the attribute of chesed, named in the verse "To You, Havaya, is the greatness"
the sefira of foundation, through which the flow passes to Malchus
the spiritual flow that comes through the *galgalim* and the constellations, from its root
faith; here, the true understanding and faith in G-d's essence, which transcends everything

blocks.text: The class opens with a recap. The last chapters taught how to contemplate: go the length and the width to reach depth in *bina* and then *chachma*, and see how *daas* works in that. They worked an example, *memalei kol almin*, the light that fills all worlds, through Reb Hillel's commentary on chapter 3, and through the tract on the nature of *Chassidus*, which is another example of putting together a *yichud*. He goes back over this because he does not want to keep s*ayin*g how to make a *yichud* without first giving the context of what it is for.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 044 ch 4 part 1.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: The opening of the class, before line 1 is read: a recap of the earlier chapters and why he recaps.

blocks.text: Now the question is the method. Having some sense of how the process works, the question is which way to go: by the general themes, or by deep, specific examples. In the tract on *Chassidus* the Rebbe gives one particular example, a *yichud* on *Modeh Ani*, which is the particular way, and it can be made more detailed still. Reb Hillel's explanation of the nine *meshalim* for *memalei kol almin* is general, though more detailed than before, because it lays out all the levels and how they relate. The nine *meshalim* for *memalei kol almin* began as one general idea. Through *iyun* one sees a lower perspective of *etzem* and *hispashtus*, then finds that idea in oneself as *daas*, and then reaches the depth of the higher perspective, *gilui ha'helem*. So there is a sliding scale, from more general to more specific.

blocks.title: The root of a plant
blocks.text: In *Torah*, and especially in the discourses, the words for root, principle and source each carry a different relationship, and he takes the root. A plant's root draws its nutrients from the power of growth in the ground, which is common to all plants. That power is narrowed and filtered until it becomes the power that grows this particular plant. The root is the abstract source, more general than the particulars, and in their root they are all the same.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 044 ch 4 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: Take *memalei kol almin*, G-d filling all three worlds, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*. It can be explained in a general way: it is all one root, with no real difference in how G-d is in each of the three worlds.

blocks.text: All the different metaphors, of the light of the sun, of extensions and expressions, and of the letters of speech, are in general one idea: the revelation of what was hidden.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 044 ch 4 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The general idea here is the relation of a created, limited being to an unlimited Creator. The world is a limited creation, an expression of the infinite Creator. There are many ways of putting this and many *meshalim*, but all of it is still the general idea.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 044 ch 4 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: Reb Hillel's details are still about the general theme. What the class has not yet done is take particular examples: how an apple would be seen at the level of *Asiya*, of *Yetzira*, of *Beriya* and of *Atzilus*, and back down again. There is a lot of that inside this theme, and most of the book is going to be about it.

In its general form, what is the light of *Atzilus*, and what is its *tzimtzum* from the Essence? How incomparable are the *sefiros* of *Atzilus* to the essence of the Emanator, who transcends even the ten *sefiros* and contains infinite ones?

blocks.text: Also: how G-d is one with the lights of *Atzilus*. He unites with them, and His essence is expressed through them, though they are far lower than He is. There are many particular details to this, and the book will go through them level by level along the chain of descent. The aim, perhaps, is to learn the book again and again, so that the *meshalim* are understood. That is the *haskala* of *Chassidus*, it seems.

blocks.title: The coal in the flame
blocks.text: There are many metaphors for this. One is a coal inside a flame, inside a coal, which *Sefer Yetzira* mentions: blow on it and it is revealed. Another is how the faculties of the soul are revealed from the soul's essence, in the general way. He says the class has covered many of these with Reb Hillel.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 044 ch 4 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: Once you have studied the metaphors, and seen how each contributes and how they differ, you arrive at a much deeper understanding of the general idea. That is the lower unity, which in general is *memalei kol almin*. *Hisbonenus* requires *iyun*: you must learn the detailed explanations. Within that, one can focus on the abstract structure of the chain of descent, or on how it applies to particular things, as with the example of *Modeh Ani*, a very particular experience of waking up in the morning.

sections.summary: The general way gives depth and the particular way gives nearness; each is needed, and the teaching is to join them.

blocks.text: The Talmud's famous expression for two things, each with an advantage the other lacks, is that one is not like the other. So we really need a little of both.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 044 ch 4 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The general way has its advantage: it reaches the depth in the general. In any subject one needs to generalize what one learns. One of the core ideas of *Understanding by Design*, a curriculum-design theory he worked with, is that understanding means a student can generalize what he learns and apply it to something new.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 044 ch 4 part 1.mp3

blocks.title: The Pilgrims
blocks.text: Take a history lesson on the Pilgrims coming to America. You select the big themes and questions: what it is to move and make a transition in life, why people do it, what the opportunities are, what is hard about it. Then you show how these apply to other areas of life. When a student can apply them, that is the proof of understanding. That is the general way: find the big idea, and see that whatever you study is an example of it. If you get the general point, you have the real depth of it.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 044 ch 4 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: So we want this depth in the general: not seeing G-dliness in one aspect of the world, but appreciating G-dliness in general, which is the essence of the G-dly light.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 044 ch 4 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The aim is to appreciate the essential G-dly life, which encompasses everything and transcends any one example or expression, as the tract on *Chassidus* shows. Both steps are needed: first identify and understand the transcendent generality, then see how it permeates the specifics. Doing both is what he is describing for learning *Chassidus*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 044 ch 4 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: Without that, you stay at one level of how a teaching is read, the plain sense, the hint, the homily or the secret, or within one world. You understand it there but do not see how it connects to G-d's real unity. The aim is to see G-d's unity, not only to learn about a certain angel or a certain *sefira*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 044 ch 4 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The Mitteler Rebbe, in his introduction to *Amrei Binah*, says that a person who learns about all the levels without seeing how they unite in G-d's simple essence has the opposite of the whole point. The point of learning is to see how everything unites in that one general point, which is all part of the transcendent, essential unity.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 044 ch 4 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The ultimate goal is the revelation of G-dliness in the soul: an awareness and appreciation of this essence, which transcends any particular creation and which we can find all around us, in ourselves and in other people. That is the advantage of learning in the general way.

blocks.text: There is an advantage to the particular way as well: it shows how G-dliness permeates a particular example of something around us. The Rebbe did this, explaining in general and in theory the idea of *yechida* and how it is transcendent, and then giving a particular example, *Modeh Ani*, which takes that general idea and applies it to one particular experience in the world around us.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 044 ch 4 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The advantage is that the revelation of G-dliness becomes very close and relevant to you: something you really experience, can see and can point to in your life, not an abstraction or a theory. That is a grasp of the essence itself, not only knowing that it exists, the way one knows a theory. The com*bina*tion of both is the perfection of *Moshiach*: the general that transcends, and the particular that permeates. Then one sees G-d's essence in the world, as the verse says, all flesh will see G-d as one. The Rebbe stresses that "see" does not mean only with the eye: every one of the senses is transformed into experience of G-dliness.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 044 ch 4 part 1.mp3

blocks.question: What is the advantage of the particular way?

blocks.text: Someone who studies only in the general way can fool himself, and think that the matter is very close to him, when it is very far. He can imagine he has a very close understanding and really gets it.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 044 ch 4 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The most extreme case is someone who does no *hisbonenus* at all. He takes only the general *meshalim* of how G-d fills the world, like the light of the sun, a candle, or a soul filling a body, and uses his imagination to picture G-d as a spirit filling everything around him.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 044 ch 4 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The Alter Rebbe's discourse on this describes all kinds of delusions it causes, even hallucinations, and it is not a healthy thing to do. Even a person who really studies in depth, and understands the differences between the *meshalim*, can fool himself if he only learns the framework of the chain of descent and never applies it to particular things, as the Rebbe applied it to *Modeh Ani*. He knows the words and their metaphors, talks very intelligently, and believes he is very close.

blocks.text: It is a theory he knows and is familiar with, the abstract part of it, but he does not see how to apply it at all. At the end of chapter 3 the Mitteler Rebbe complained that many chassidim, because they lacked the power of *tevuna* to apply what they understood, felt that *Chassidus* and *avoda* were two separate things and did not see how to apply them. The same thing happens here: a person can fool himself into thinking that the matter is very near.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 044 ch 4 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: Line 14 says that G-d is seen from very far off by someone who understands only in the general way. The image is borrowed from Avraham on the way to the Akeidah, who saw the spirit of Hashem over the mountain from far. Such a person's understanding is only abstract and theoretical, so he cannot apply it, and it does not change how he sees his day-to-day life.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 044 ch 4 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: On the other hand, the particular way: take a particular topic, a particular experience or aspect of life, as the Rebbe does with *Modeh Ani* or any discourse. It takes some work to mine it, but then the insight is life-changing, something you can relate to, feel and see. It is more limited than the general, but within its scope it is very tangible.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 044 ch 4 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: This is the same in any educational theory. You start with the tangible, grounded experience, and from there contemplate and come to appreciate *chachma*, which is the generalization. The idea then becomes firmly implanted in the soul: close in the sense of relevant, and known from direct experience.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 044 ch 4 part 1.mp3

blocks.title: The classroom and the years of experience
blocks.text: You build step by step, from the particular to a higher particular, until you grasp the general in its full generality. Then you are not fooling yourself at all. Compare someone who learns in a classroom with someone who has years of experience. The second has particular examples where the ideas were in action, and from those he builds up the big ideas. He really knows it.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 044 ch 4 part 1.mp3

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 044 ch 4 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: It can take a long time. A lot of this is plain science, about things in the world and how they work. It is not G-dly in itself, which is why some people shy away from it, since the details seem not to be G-dly. But understood in the context of the purpose, it all connects.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 044 ch 4 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: Then he takes the particular *ofanim* of *Asiya*, then the *Chayos* they come from, then the highest angels of *Asiya*, until he reaches *Malchus* of *Asiya*: the general G-dly light that makes up the world of *Asiya*. Because he has already gone through the *galgalim* and the angels, he is able to appreciate that general light.

Even though each detail on its own is not really a G-dly thing, G-dliness is not openly apparent in a physical thing, an angel or a *sefira*. It is like the levels of a teaching, where much is not openly apparent: the essence is there. Studied that way, the detail can be detached from seeing G-d's unity, and that is the problem.

When you put all this study together, and see how the details connect back to the general theme and express it, you really understand the general point. It transcends all the parts and is in certain ways more important than them. But you can only get that generality truly through learning all the details. blocks.text: On the other hand, the general way alone: as he said before, a person who only does the general *hisbonenus* sees G-d only from far. He does not truly understand it in a way that is relatable and experiential.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 044 ch 4 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: It is abstract theory, what I call psychobabble: people like to say these words, but what does it mean? It could mean anything. Without concrete understanding it has no grounding in experience.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 044 ch 4 part 1.mp3

sensitivity.reason: A dismissive label, "psychobabble", for people who talk abstractly.
sensitivity.publishable: It is abstract theory: people like to say these words, but what does it mean? It could mean anything. Without concrete understanding it has no grounding in experience.

blocks.text: Each approach has an advantage and a disadvantage. The advantage of the general is that one gets the main points, and the general *hisbonenus* is the main thing; but that is true only if it comes after detailed, specific study. A person who only does the general thinks he is seeing G-d from close, when in truth he is seeing Him from very far. He thinks he understands, but it is a delusion.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Such a person can fall into false fantasies, like fools and people who lack understanding. That lack is not a lack of intelligence but of maturity, the sense that comes from experience. His mind's vessel is narrowed to one thing, a general one, and he focuses on it very intensely, until he thinks he sees angels or that G-d is speaking to him.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The Alter Rebbe has a very short discourse, one of two on *hisbonenus* in his book of short discourses, the *Kitzurim*, that describes this: the focus, the excitement and emotion, the spiritual high, and all of it a delusion. Real understanding is a grounded, step-by-step process. Real spiritual experience comes as inspiration only once in a while.

blocks.text: Deepening attention in each detail is the opposite of error and distance. *Ha'amakas hadaas* means focusing one's attention and relating it personally, finding it in yourself. When you do that with the details, it is something you can really understand directly.

blocks.title: The gratitude journal
blocks.text: Not "all is one and one is all," repeated until you feel it, which is not real. Take a particular matter, like the attribute of judgment or gratitude. People who keep a gratitude journal and work on it, focusing and internalizing, are doing something very productive, because it is real and grounded in experience. That is the opposite of fooling oneself. In any field of work, you get real experience by going out and doing it.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: On the contrary, by this the matter comes nearer to a person. By focusing on the details and really connecting to them, it becomes very near, something the person really understands. He goes from one detail to the next higher detail, in an orderly way,

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Going from *Asiya* to *Yetzira* to *Beriya* to *Atzilus*, one builds the structure on that foundation, until all the details are united in one general *yichud klali*; then the whole process is true. Someone who is hyper-focused on one little detail, and never sees how it fits the whole collective, does not have the big picture.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: For example, a particular *yichud* on "To You, *Havaya*, is *gedula*": the kindness we see in the world is really coming from *Havaya*. Look around, see the greatness and the kindness in the world, trace it up, and see how it comes from *Havaya*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

sections.title: Yichud: the unity, and what its parts are
sections.summary: Yichud is the depth of grasp of *bittul*; the particular unities and the general unity each have a place in the chain of descent.

phrases.en: So this idea of the *yichud* is

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: they will eventually come to have a deep understanding

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: of the *bittul*

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: היש לאין ביחודא עילאה ויחודא תתאה
phrases.en: how the *yesh* that we see in the world is really coming from this abstract, g-dly source, both on the lower unity and the upper unity

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Yichud, the unity of G-dliness, is the depth of grasp in the *bittul* of *yesh* into *ayin*, in both the upper and the lower unity. One arrives at it by detailed *hisbonenus*: understanding each step with all the *meshalim* needed to build the unity, until one sees how the *yesh* we see in the world comes from the abstract, G-dly source.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: and then you can make a specific *yichud*

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: on a particular thing

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: for example, like we said, "To You, Havaya, is *gedula*"

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת חסד שבמלכות דאצילות בבי''ע
phrases.en: is the kindness of the *chesed* of *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, the way that's coming into *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: but you can see how that comes down to each detail in each world

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: that's only one particular example of how G-d relates to the world

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: and then a person does a separate *yichud* on "To You, Havaya, is *gevura*"

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: both the general idea of how all *gevura* comes from Havaya, and also seeing all the particular examples

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: that's another specific *yichud*, seeing how G-d's *gevura* extends to all the worlds

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: ועל דרך זה בכל יחודים פרטיים שבי׳ ספירות דבי''ע כידוע
phrases.en: and same thing with all the particular unifications that a person can make of seeing how all the ten *sefiros* are expressed in the different worlds of *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*, as you know

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: A particular *yichud* on a particular thing: as in "To You, *Havaya*, is *gedula*", which is the *chesed* of *Malchus* of *Atzilus* coming into the lower three worlds. This is still fairly general, but you can see how it comes down into each detail in each world.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: When you contemplate it, you do not just think, all the greatness is G-d's. You look at particular examples: how does this show in *Asiya*, in *Yetzira*, in *Beriya*, in *Atzilus*? You trace it up. Even then it is only one example of how G-d relates to the world, the *chesed* of *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, as opposed to the general relationship of *Malchus*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Another particular *yichud*, on "To You, *Havaya*, is *gevura*": how all *gevura* comes from *Havaya*, in general and in particulars, and the difference between each as it appears in *Asiya*, *Yetzira* and *Beriya*. Take the example of *Modeh Ani*: the *yichud* of two *middos*, *Malchus* and *Yesod*, which in *Asiya* is gratitude for the waking experience, and in *Yetzira* is recognizing that the world is created new every moment. So each *yichud* looks a little different in each world.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: There are many more of this kind. One *yichud* can be about food in general, which includes fruit and bread, and another just about fruit; there is a difference, and places in Torah, *Chassidus* and *Kabbalah* discuss these. The *gevura* extending to all the worlds is another specific one.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The same goes for all the particular unifications of the ten *sefiros* of *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*: seeing how the ten *sefiros* are expressed in each of the three worlds.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: But then the idea of a general *yichud*

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: הוא כמו מה שכתוב הנה מקום אתי
phrases.en: It says, "Behold, the place," the entire idea of place is all with Me

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: או המלך המרומם כו' המתנשא מכל ימות עולם
phrases.en: or how G-d is a King that transcends the world, and so, even though G-d is like the King of the world, but He really transcends it, that He transcends all the days of the world

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: the both the *middos* and the intellect or the *mochin* that's related to those *middos*

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: וגם זה פרט יחשב לגבי עצמות בחינת המלכות
phrases.en: and even this general *yichud* of seeing how everything is all of time and space is *batel* to Havaya is considered a detail compared to the general essence of the idea of *Malchus*

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: which is the *Keser* of *Malchus*

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The general *yichud* is like the verse "Behold, the place is with Me." After seeing how all the particular *middos* are united, one recognizes that the whole idea of time and space, and of the *middos* and *Malchus* and everything, is *batel* to Hashem. That is the general *yichud*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: G-d is a King who transcends the world. Even though He is like the King of the world, He really transcends it, and He transcends all the days of the world. That means He transcends the *middos* of our world, both time and space, and the hierarchy that relates to the *middos*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The *middos*, and the intellect, the *mochin*, which relates to those *middos*: the *chachma* and *bina* in them. He discusses this at length elsewhere, in *Amrei Binah*, in great depth.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Even this general *yichud*, seeing how everything, time and space, is *batel* to Hashem, is a detail compared to the general essence of *Malchus*, the *Keser* of *Malchus*. That is not *Malchus* as it creates a world, but its essence: the way it expresses G-d's will and His essence.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: and we have a similar thing with all the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus*

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: עד עצמות בחינת מלכות דאין סוף
phrases.en: and tracing how they all connect all the way up to *Malchus* of *Ein Sof*

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: at the beginning of that original line of light that's at the beginning of the process of creation

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: there's many, many particular unifications

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: ויחוד הכללי בכללות ביטול כל ההשתלשלות דקו כו'
phrases.en: and that is the general *yichud* of seeing how the entire *seder hishtalshelus*, the entire process of creation with all of its worlds, are all nullified and to G-d, and they're all just an expression of Him and one with Him

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: לגבי עצמות אור אין סוף כידוע.
phrases.en: how they relate to the essence of the infinite light, as is known

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The same with the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus*: trace them up to *Malchus* of *Ein Sof*, at the start of the original line of light. There are many particular *yichudim* in each *sefira* and each detail, each with its own unity and G-dly expression, a real expression of G-d's essence. Each one is done separately to get the whole picture.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The general *yichud* is the nullification of the whole chain of creation, the whole process of the line of light, to the essence of the infinite light. All of it is an expression of Him and one with Him.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: If one only does the general *yichudim*, one fools oneself and does not understand properly. If one only does the detailed ones, each detail is not necessarily a G-dly thing. So the approach is to focus on the details and the specifics, as a foundation to build up the complete understanding of the big picture, uniting everything into a bigger framework.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

sections.title: The general needs the details, and the details need the general
sections.summary: Starting from the general without the details does not take hold in the soul; the two need each other, as a word needs its context. The class then turns to the old dispute over where the focus lies in davening: on the meaning of the words, or on who one is standing before.

phrases.he: אך הנה מי שלא העמיק דעתו ביחודים פרטים ומתחיל מבחינת הכלל,
phrases.en: but if a person will not focus first on these particular unifications and they'll just start with the general idea

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: even though they're going to work very hard

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: בהשגות רבות באיכות ענין הביטול בכלל,
phrases.en: and study it, and study all the *meshalim*, and really go over it until they understand it as best as they can

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: the flame to the coal, and this kind of thing, these kind of ideas

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: לא יוקבע בנפשו אמיתית ענינו כל כך,
phrases.en: he's not going to really be able to appreciate the true idea of what we mean by this G-d's unity

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: כמו אחר עיון היטב בכל פרטיים,
phrases.en: as he would be able to really appreciate it after, and really understand it clearly, after studying all of the details

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: And if from those details you come and arrive at that general idea, then it's much more true

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: והיינו דפרט אצטריך לכלל וכלל אצטריך לפרט,
phrases.en: And this is the idea that the details need the general reality and the generality needs the details

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: מפני שאין כלל בלא פרט כו'
phrases.en: because you can't really have a *klal* without the details

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Someone who did not first deepen in particular unifications, and starts from the general idea, may work very hard and study all the *meshalim*, even the flame and the coal. Still, the idea is not fixed in his soul as firmly as after studying every detail.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: He will not really grasp what we mean by G-d's unity, the way he would after studying all the details. Only if from those details he arrives at the general idea is it much more true.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: This is the nature of intellect: any model or theory meant to represent something is never able to capture its full truth. The real reality is in experience, the particular things you have in the physical world, and a mental model has no meaning unless it is grounded in them. There is no substitute for experience. It is a different level of understanding when you experience something firsthand.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: A list with the title "A Kite"
blocks.text: Take a list of random sentences that people are asked to memorize. They seem random and are hard to remember. Then the same list is shown with a title on top, "A Kite", and suddenly they all make sense and are easy to remember, since you know what they are about. So details without the general lack cohesion. And the reverse: the general alone is ethereal, without substance, because the words have no grounding.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: (ודבר זה כבר נחלקו בו הרבה מגדולי הראשונים
phrases.en: And this discussion is not just something that relates to *Kabbalah* or whatever. This is actually a *machlokes* in *rishonim*, the halachic authorities of the Middle Ages, debating about the proper way of having *kavana* in davening.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: for example, this is a debate between the Rambam and the Tur

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: אם לכוון בפירוש המלות דרך פרט בגדלות יהו״ה,
phrases.en: should a person focus on the meaning of the words mainly and think about the particular praises of Hashem that we're speaking about there

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: אם לכוון דרך כלל, לפני מי אתה עומד
phrases.en: or should it mainly be focused on recognizing who I'm standing in front of

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: as explained in the Chassidic manuscripts

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Which of the two is the proper *kavana* in davening is a real dispute among the early authorities of the Middle Ages. For example, the Rambam and the Tur debate whether, in the meaning of the words, one should focus on the particular praises of Hashem, or, in general, on who one is standing before. This is not only a question for *Kabbalah*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: He says this was explained in the Chassidic writings. At that time there was no printed *Chassidus*. It was copied by hand and shared among people, and the Alter Rebbe's longer discourses from later in his life were called the writings.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.question: Which is the main focus when davening: the meaning of the words and the particular praises, or the recognition of who one is standing before?

sections.title: Keep the intention on the essence, and the practice for the new
sections.summary: The intention of all study is G-d's essence; the details of *Kabbalah* serve it; a newcomer starts with the general, and the one who prays keeps his intention on Him.

phrases.he: והגם שהמחשבה כללית עם המחשבה פרטית לא ישכנו כאחד,
phrases.en: even though we have this problem that you can't be thinking about both at the same time: either you're thinking about the general idea, or you're thinking about the details

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: מכל מקום מי שהוא מעמיק בכל לבו ובכל חפצו לעצמות האלקות דוקא,
phrases.en: but if a person, if their intention and their real, sincere goal in studying *Chassidus* and all these topics is with all their heart and soul they just want to connect to G-d's essence, that's what they really want

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: even when they're studying the details and the particulars

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: יכוין הכל אל המחשבה הכללית דעצמות דוקא
phrases.en: they'll be able to direct everything and aim everything towards the general point

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: and will never become distracted from the general true point of everything

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: by focusing his *kavana* in the details, that is not going to distract him and make him forget about what is the real priority

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: מאחר שכל הפרטים אינם נמשכים והולכים רק אחר הכלל דוקא,
phrases.en: because the entire purpose of his studying the particulars is all as a result of and as an outcome of trying to understand the general, the big picture

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: כידוע לכל הולך בדרך אמת, ליהו״ה לבדו דוקא,
phrases.en: as is known to anyone who is truthfully, sincerely walking to come close to Hashem, and that's all they just want to know G-d

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: כמו שכתבו זכרונם לברכה אליו ולא למדותיו
phrases.en: like our Sages of blessed memory have said, that when you pray it should be to Him and not to His *middos*

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: General thought and particular thought cannot be together; one has to pick. What matters is the intention: if a person's whole heart and goal in studying *Chassidus* is to connect to G-d's essence, that is what counts. The Mitteler Rebbe stresses this in his introduction to *Amrei Binah*: if someone only wants to know the levels and the names of angels, as a lot of Kabbalists do, that can be the opposite of the purpose and a distraction.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

sensitivity.reason: A sweeping remark about Kabbalists who study the levels and the angels for their own sake.
sensitivity.publishable: General thought and particular thought cannot be together; one has to pick. blocks.text: If a person sincerely wants to know G-d's unity, he learns these things to see how they connect to G-d and how G-d is there, not so that he can say, "Look, I know the secrets," and show off that he is a big Kabbalist. That is the opposite of the point.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

sensitivity.reason: A jab at Kabbalists who want to show off what they know.
sensitivity.publishable: If a person sincerely wants to know G-d's unity, he learns these things to see how they connect to G-d and how G-d is there, not so that he can say, "Look, I know the secrets," and show off what he knows. That is the opposite of the point.

blocks.text: Even when he studies the details, a person aims everything at the one general point. The general is in the back of his mind while he works on the particulars, but he never loses track of it, because that is his whole motivation.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: His intention will not fall from the general point while he focuses on particular details, because the details are studied only as a way of reaching the general.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: As is known to anyone who truly walks the path, he wants G-d alone. The Sages say that when you pray it should be to Him and not to His *middos*: you pray to Him, not to His attributes.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The Arizal's *kavanos* do speak of all these levels, and part of what he means is that they can be a distraction, if a person thinks about names and levels and *sefiros* and forgets G-d. That is what we do not want to happen.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: *Hayom Yom* says to daven with the Arizal's *kavanos* only if one understands them and knows how to put them in context. Just thinking of names and letters is a distraction. When the intention is only to know G-d and see His essence, and one studies within that context, it is all right.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: רק כללות ענין ההתבוננות בפרטי מדותיו הוא רק כדי שיבא לעצמותו ומהותו דוקא
phrases.en: the entire idea of studying these the details of G-d's *middos* is only in order to come to know that His essence and His true nature

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: ולא לכוון העיקר רק בכוונה של הפרט,
phrases.en: not to make the main purpose or a person's main intention shouldn't just be to think about all these like as if it's like a spell or an incantation

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: like as if it's just its own separate subject, its own topic, just to learn angelology and learn about whatever

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The whole idea of studying the details of G-d's *middos* is to come to know His essence and true nature. The main intention may not be the detail itself, as if it were a spell or an incantation: think this name and then that angel, say this and do that. That is the opposite of the whole purpose, and it is how many people take *Kabbalah*, as if it were magic. Nor should it be its own subject, like learning angelology just to learn about whatever.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: גם בעיונו בספר הזוהר ובכתבי האריז''ל
phrases.en: and even when a person is studying the *Zohar* and the works of the *Arizal*

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: צריך להיות על דרך זה דוקא
phrases.en: a person has to study that with the same approach

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: (וכאשר מקובל היה אבי אדוני מורי ורבי זכרונו לברכה נשמתו עדן בדבר זה מפי הרב המגיד
phrases.en: that my father, the *Alter Rebbe*, received from the Maggid of Mezeritch

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: בפירוש גמור וכך שמעתי מפיו זכרונו לברכה)
phrases.en: and I heard this from my father, the *Alter Rebbe*, and he explained this very clearly directly to me

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The same goes for the *Zohar* and the writings of the *Arizal*: they must be studied with the same approach, not as *Kabbalah* on its own, separate from G-d's unity. G-d forbid.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: The approach from the Maggid
blocks.text: The Alter Rebbe received this approach from the Maggid of Mezeritch. The author, speaking in the first person, heard it from his father, the Alter Rebbe, who explained it very clearly and directly to him. The approach is that the details are studied only as part of connecting to the general idea of recognizing G-d's unity.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: There was a whole debate at that time about whether people should learn *Kabbalah* at all, or should simply have faith. When people overly intellectualize it, with maps and charts, it distracts them from the main point. But done properly, it gives great richness and brings a person's faith in the inner dimension, where he really understands and knows, not just believes. Chabad's approach has always been to put the two together this way.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: and this is the answer to those that ask

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: how is it that people that know, if let's say they know these particular

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: ליודעים בהם, איך שאינם מבלבלים את מחשבת הכלל
phrases.en: how does that not distract them from this general intention that they're davening to G-d? It seems like a distraction

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: On the contrary

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: כוונות פירוש המלות על פי המלות עפ"י הקבלה
phrases.en: if a person knows how to do it properly, then start see having these particular kavanos in davening according to Kabbalah, like according to the *Arizal*

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: מסייעים לחזק את עומק השגת הכלל בעצמות אלקות,
phrases.en: actually strengthens their ability to really understand the general appreciation of G-dliness

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: כידוע לטועמי טעם בהם דרך פרט כו'
phrases.en: as it's known to anybody that has tasted them of studying it in a detailed way

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: but for somebody that's new to this whole study

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: יותר טוב להם להעמיק דרך כלל תחלה,
phrases.en: a person should first focus on the general and think about these general *kavanos*

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: עד שיורגלו מעט מעט בדרך הפרט דווקא ודי למבין:
phrases.en: and they should slowly become accustomed to seeing how that general idea is found and expressed in the details

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: This answers the question of how people who know the particular meanings of the words, according to *Kabbalah* or *Chassidus*, are not distracted from the general intention they have when they daven to G-d. It seems like a distraction.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: On the contrary: when a person knows how to do it properly, the *kavanos* of the words, according to *Kabbalah* and the Arizal, help strengthen the depth of the grasp of the general, the unity of G-dliness. Anyone who has tasted this in detailed study knows it.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: For someone new to all this, it is better to deepen in the general way first, and think about these general *kavanos*, until he is slowly accustomed to the particular path. The Rebbe, in the tract on *Chassidus*, first breaks us out of our concept of the details to see a general essence higher than them, and then brings us back down to see that essence expressed in all the details. So first one needs a strong, if somewhat abstract, grasp of the general point. Then, seeing it applied in the details, one gets a rich, deep, personal understanding of that *klal*, connected to it and not a distraction.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The approach starts from the top, as the Arizal does too, with G-d's essence that transcends everything, the essence of the infinite light before the *tzimtzum*, which is the general. Then we see how it comes down and permeates all the details. Afterwards, the descending flows are mostly from the bottom up and then back down again.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The basic approach: keep the big picture in mind. There is only G-d, and all these levels are Him choosing to express Himself, with nothing separate from Him. With that in mind, learn the details and see how they connect back and express that essence. The objective is not to make lists and maps and memorize names and *meshalim*, which can be very distracting from the point.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: The child's intention
blocks.text: The Gemara says that someone prays with the intention of a little child, who pictures G-d as an invisible king standing before him, whom he can ask for anything and who will help him. Such a simple picture is so close to the truth that you can call it the truth. He humanizes G-d in his imagery, but he does not limit Him: he knows G-d is infinite and beyond anything.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: On the other hand, someone sits davening and thinks about *Adam Kadmon* and the highest level of the chain, and he thinks he has G-d figured out. He limits G-d to this intellectual idea, even though it is a very high, lofty one, and that is so close to *avoda zara* that you can actually call it *avoda zara*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 04/Shaar HaYichud 045 ch 4 part 2.mp3

sensitivity.reason: A sharp Chassidic judgment that an intellectual picture of G-d while davening is avoda zara; "you can actually call it avoda zara" is the sharp form of the teaching.
sensitivity.publishable: On the other hand, someone sits davening and thinks about *Adam Kadmon* and the highest level of the chain, and he thinks he has G-d figured out. He limits G-d to this intellectual idea, even though it is a very high, lofty one, and that is so close to *avoda zara*.

blocks.text: What to watch for: we learn about the chain of descent, *Kabbalah* and *Chassidus*, but the whole idea is to keep the essence (*yechida*) in mind and see how everything expresses it, and not let the *yechida* get trapped in any of these garments. Instead we see that those are expressing the *yechida*. That is the idea.
